mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which compresses earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four-month INDPRO contractions below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 5-year averages signals a stagflationary environment, which increases uncertainty and discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 5-year averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in demand drivers, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS and HOUST fall for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS accelerates above 0.5% MoM for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and sustained rebound in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months, combined with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE), signals a supply-side recovery that boosts earnings and reduces recession risk, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA for five consecutive months AND UNRATE < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during five-month INDPRO rebounds above 12-month MA with falling UNRATE.
